expected_output.reasoning: The investigation identifies all three expected malicious patterns with matching details: (1) sqlmap scanner from 198.51.100.60, ~225 requests, all blocked by CommonRuleSet UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER; (2) sensitive-path scan from 198.51.100.20, 225 distinct URIs (including /.git, backup paths, wp-config, etc.), mostly allowed (~200/225) because baseline rules only match traversal/restricted extensions; (3) card-testing burst of POST /checkout/payment from 198.51.100.30 (~1,350 requests), allowed because the rate-based rule is in Count mode (detected, not blocked). It also correctly identifies the Artillery load-test client 198.51.100.10 as benign automation rather than an attack, and explains why the rate rule must stay in Count (to avoid blocking the benign automation) while recommending a scoped rate rule for /checkout/payment. This matches the expected root cause closely in substance, causal chain, and key identifying details (IPs, request counts, rule names, timestamps).
expected_output.evidence: "sqlmap SQLi scan fully blocked: Client 198.51.100.60 (UA sqlmap/1.8.2#stable) sent 225 requests... all 225 BLOCKED... terminated by CommonRuleSet UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER" ; "Client 198.51.100.20 ran a path-scanning / forced-browsing spree: 225 requests across 225 distinct URIs... WAF blocked only 25... The remaining 200 recon probes were ALLOWED to origin" ; "Client 198.51.100.30 sent 1,350 POST /checkout/payment in ~50s... all ALLOWED... the rate-based rule only Counts" ; "198.51.100.10 accounts for 99.01% of traffic... A benign load generator, and the reason the global rate rule must remain in Count."

assertion_results.text: A Cause finding reports the sqlmap client 198.51.100.60 with about 225 requests, all blocked by UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER (a much smaller count, such as a few dozen, does not pass)
assertion_results.evidence: "Client 198.51.100.60 (UA sqlmap/1.8.2#stable) sent 225 requests, 17:03:37–17:13:10, peak 27/min — all 225 BLOCKED, 0 allowed, every one terminated by CommonRuleSet UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER" matches ~225 requests, all blocked by UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER.

assertion_results.text: A Cause finding reports the sensitive-path scan from 198.51.100.20 with its volume: about 225 requests to about 225 distinct URIs, most of them (roughly 185 to 200) allowed and only a small share (roughly 25 to 40) blocked. A much smaller total, such as about 50 requests, or a statement that the scan was mostly blocked, does not pass
assertion_results.evidence: "225 requests across 225 distinct URIs ... WAF blocked only 25 ... The remaining 200 recon probes were ALLOWED to origin" — 225 requests/URIs, ~25 blocked, ~200 allowed, matching the asserted ranges.

assertion_results.text: A Cause finding identifies a card-testing burst of POST requests to /checkout/payment from 198.51.100.30 and states the rate-based rule only counted it (Count mode), so it was detected but not blocked
assertion_results.evidence: "Client 198.51.100.30 sent 1,350 POST /checkout/payment in ~50s ... all ALLOWED ... but the rate-based rule only Counts (458 count matches recorded, no Block). ... the rate rule is non-enforcing" directly states detection without block due to Count mode.

assertion_results.text: The high-volume load-test client 198.51.100.10 (Artillery) is described as known automation (in a Supporting Observation, a hypothesis, or the Root Cause), and no Cause finding classifies it as an attack, abuse, a flood or card testing
assertion_results.evidence: The Artillery client is described in a Supporting Observation: "99% of traffic is an Artillery load-test IP ... A benign load generator, and the reason the global rate rule must remain in Count." No Cause finding classifies it as attack/abuse/flood/card testing; the two Cause findings about card testing refer to 198.51.100.30, not 198.51.100.10.

assertion_results.text: The Root Cause gives an overall assessment covering what WAF blocked (the sqlmap injection) and what it missed and why (the path scan matched no rule; the card testing was only counted because the rate-based rule is in Count), and its mitigations are separated into WAF-layer and application-layer measures
assertion_results.evidence: The Root Cause states: "it cleanly stops signature-obvious tooling (sqlmap via the BadBots header) but its managed URI-path rules cover only traversal and restricted extensions, leaving well-formed sensitive-path recon unmatched, and its only volumetric control (the P1 IP rate rule) is in Count, so a card-testing-shaped payment burst was merely counted... closing it (path-scoped, Count-first rules) is what stops recurrence." This covers blocked/missed reasons but does not explicitly separate mitigations into WAF-layer vs application-layer categories; it mentions only WAF-layer fixes (path-scoped, Count-first rules) with no application-layer mitigation discussed.

assertion_results.text: No finding recommends switching the site-wide rate-based rule to Block; the Root Cause or its mitigations state that it should stay in Count because it would block the known-automation client
assertion_results.evidence: The 'Cause: Rate-based rule in Count mode lets volumetric abuse through' finding states: "Switching the rule to Block (or adding a tighter per-IP rate rule on /checkout/payment) would stop volumetric payment abuse." This directly recommends switching the rate-based rule to Block, contradicting the assertion that no finding recommends this.
